summary: Karl Friedrich Geldner worked in Indology and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at Leipzig and Tübingen under Rudolf von Roth, Hermann Brockhaus, and Ernst Windisch. He taught at Tübingen, Halle-Wittenberg, Berlin (1890), and Marburg (1907–1921).
Karl G. Heider studied at Williams College (~1952–1953), Harvard College (~1953–1956), and Harvard University (~1957–1966).

Karl H. Potter was an Indologist and philosopher. He studied at the University of California and at Harvard under Daniel H. H. Ingalls. He served at Minnesota, Washington (~1971–1997), and as General Editor of the Encyclopedia of Indian Philosophies.

Karl Hoffmann worked in Indology, linguistics, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied under Ferdinand Sommer and Walther Wüst. He held chairs at Saarland University (1952–1955) and Erlangen-Nuremberg (1955–1983) and joined the Bavarian Academy of Sciences in 1972.

Karl Jettmar worked in history, archaeology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and Indology. He earned his doctorate at Vienna, where he later taught, and held posts at Weltmuseum Wien, Mainz (1961), and Heidelberg University (1964–1986).

Karl Joseph Hieronymus Windischmann worked in philosophy and Indology. He studied at Mainz and Würzburg. He taught at Gymnasium and Lyceum Aschaffenburg (1803) before becoming a professor of medicine at the University of Bonn in 1818.

Karl Lachmann worked in linguistics. He studied at the University of Leipzig (~1809–1812) and the University of Göttingen (~1812–1815) and held a post at Humboldt University of Berlin from around 1825 to 1851.

Karl Müllenhoff worked in linguistics, history, and archaeology. He studied at the Meldorfer Gelehrtenschule, Kiel, Leipzig, and Humboldt University of Berlin. He held posts at Kiel University (1842) and Frederick William University Berlin (1858).

Karl Otfried Müller worked in history, archaeology, and linguistics. He studied at Breslau and Berlin under August Boeckh, Friedrich Schleiermacher, and Friedrich August Wolf. He taught at Magdalenaeum Wrocław and served as professor at Göttingen from 1819.

Karl Popper was a philosopher who studied at the University of Vienna and the University of Cambridge. He held academic posts at the University of Canterbury (1937–1945), London School of Economics, King's College London, and the University of London (1949–1969).

Karl Richard Lepsius worked in history, archaeology, and linguistics. He studied at Leipzig, Göttingen, and Berlin. Lepsius held a chair at Humboldt University of Berlin (~1846–1884) and served as Chief Librarian at the Royal Library of Berlin (~1873–1884).

Karl Rosenkranz worked in philosophy. He studied at Berlin under G. W. F. Hegel, and at Halle-Wittenberg and Heidelberg. He held an extraordinariat at Halle-Wittenberg (1831) before taking a chair and rectorate at Königsberg in 1833.

Karl Verner worked in linguistics and Indology. He studied at Aarhus Katedralskole, Copenhagen, and under August Leskien. He served as librarian at Halle (~1876–1883) and became dozent for Slavic studies at Copenhagen in 1882.
Karl von Hegel worked in history and archaeology. He held academic posts at the University of Rostock (~1841–1856) and the University of Erlangen-Nuremberg (~1856–1893).

Karl-Heinz Brodbeck worked in philosophy and Buddhist studies. He studied at Augsburg and the University of Munich. He held posts at Munich (1978–1988), the Munich School of Politics and Public Policy, and Würzburg-Schweinfurt (1992–2014).

Karl-Heinz Everding is a Tibetologist. He earned a PhD from the University of Bonn and completed his habilitation at the University of Hamburg, where he served as Privatdozent in 1999. He also worked at the Göttingen Academy of Sciences (~1993).
Karl-Heinz Gottmann worked in Buddhist studies. He studied under Anagarika Govinda from around 1956 to 1985 and succeeded him in 1982.
Karma Lek Shé Drayang studied under Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo and Jamgön Kongtrül Lodrö Thaye.

Karma Lekshe Tsomo works in Buddhist and religious studies. She studied under the 14th Dalai Lama and earned a PhD from the University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa. She taught at the University of San Diego (2000–2022) and Hawaiʻi (2023).

Karma Phuntsho works in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy. He studied at Oxford under Michael Aris, Richard Gombrich, and David Seyfort Ruegg, and held research posts at CNRS and the University of Cambridge.
